summary.title: hecto: Build Your Own Text Editor in Rust
summary.one_liner: You learn Rust by building a roughly 3000-line terminal text editor step by step, from raw mode input through a text viewer, editing, search, and syntax highlighting.
keywords: build a text editor in rust
learn rust by building a project
rust for engineers from other fields
takeaways: Build a minimal terminal text editor in Rust in about 3000 lines across a few files with a few dependencies.
Follow chapters covering setup, entering raw mode, raw input and output, a text viewer, a text editor, search, and syntax highlighting.
Each small step has you change code and then compile and run to see the result.
The tutorial is a re-implementation of antirez' kilo and a remix of Paige Ruten's C version, aimed at people learning Rust with or without prior Rust experience.
summary.summary: This is an introductory blog-post series in which the author walks readers through building a text editor in Rust. The editor is a re-implementation of antirez' kilo, adapted from Paige Ruten's C tutorial, and comes to roughly 3000 lines across a few files. The series is split into chapters: setup, raw mode, raw input and output, a text viewer, a text editor, search, and syntax highlighting, with appendices. Readers type in code changes step by step and observe results by compiling and running, with prose explanations that can be skipped. The page also points to the pound project by Kofi Otuo as a leaner alternative.
